mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 9% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals severe labor market weakness, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 9% and PAYEMS drops > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, leading to reduced real earnings and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% in a quarter, it signals an accommodative monetary policy supporting economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 grows > 2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% per month for three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, leading to increased consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% per month for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
